historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah (The Beginning and The End) - Volume 10, page 338 The name Saburah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: 632 AD - 661 AD (11 years after Prophet Muhammad's death)
historical_references.context: Aisha bint Abu Bakr, the wife of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), made a vow to perform a pilgrimage to Mecca and to visit the grave of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) every year if she was granted the opportunity to live. Aisha named her servant girl, Saburah, who was with her on her journey, as her heir and executor of her will. Aisha instructed Saburah to perform a pilgrimage on her behalf every year and to visit the Prophet's grave and offer prayers for her.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hadid's Sharh Nahj al-Balaghah - Volume 1, page 112 The name Saburah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Saburah is mentioned in a hadith narrated by Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) regarding serving the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his household. Saburah was a servant of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (pbuh), who was known for her generosity. One day, a poor man came to Aisha and asked for food. Aisha asked Saburah to feed him, but Saburah replied that she had already given away all the food she had. The Prophet (pbuh) overheard their conversation and instructed Saburah to prepare food for the man from his own portion of the meal. The Prophet (pbuh) then said, 'Whoever helps a believing man or woman, it is as if he has helped me.' (Sahih Muslim)
